title: UDLM Class artifact — the scoped-Class authoring layer
description: Meta-schema for a Class artifact (registry/classes/*.yaml), the authoring layer of the scoped Class hierarchy (ADR-038). It carries the FULL definition surface — elements, outputs, relationships (consumer-declared), immutable, adopts, and (type tier) context — so the compiled flat spec is complete (#323). It composes SharedDataElements (`$defs.shared_data_element`) at one tier, Base (`Machine`), Type (`Machine.VM`) or Provider (`Machine.VM.OCPVirt`), and `extends` its parent under the Liskov invariant: add or refine, never contradict. Scope position IS portability (ADR-038 §3): `portability` is derived, not asserted.

metadata.description: EXAMPLE Provider Class — not canonical: Provider Classes are provider-authored and reach canonical through the contribution lifecycle (ADR-038 authorship ruling). OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt) Provider Class for the Machine.VM Type Class. It carries only what matters on this provider: the target namespace (the ADR-016 provider-required field), instancetype/preference selection, run and eviction strategy, storage-class and boot-source mechanics, secondary-network attachments, and the GPU-passthrough / SR-IOV elements Machine.VM parks for the Provider tier. Elements are proposed pending grounding against a live VirtualMachine custom resource.

elements.description: Target OpenShift namespace for the VirtualMachine object. The request-realization enrichment step fills this from a governed layer via post-placement policy (DCM ADR-024); a consumer never names it in portable intent.

VirtualMachineClusterInstancetype name (for example u1.medium) selecting the provider's sizing bundle. When set, the provider derives vCPU and memory from the instancetype; policy validates it against the portable cpu and memory elements rather than letting the two diverge.
VirtualMachineClusterPreference name (for example fedora, windows.10) supplying guest-OS-tuned device and feature defaults.
Desired run posture of the VirtualMachine, mapped to the KubeVirt runStrategy values Always, Halted, Manual, RerunOnFailure and Once.

OpenShift StorageClass backing the VM's root and data volumes. Placement selects it from the provider's advertised classes; the consumer's portable intent speaks in storage_tier, never in a provider class name.
Boot image mechanics for this provider: a containerDisk image reference or the name of a DataVolume/PVC boot source in the target namespace.
Multus NetworkAttachmentDefinition references for secondary interfaces (for example an OVN localnet to a VLAN). Ordered; the primary pod network is implicit and never listed.
Behavior when the scheduler must vacate the node, mapped to the KubeVirt evictionStrategy values LiveMigrate, LiveMigrateIfPossible, None and External.
Host GPU devices passed through to the guest, by permitted device name. This is one of the two elements the Machine.VM flat spec deliberately excludes as Provider-Class surface (ADR-038).
SR-IOV network references for direct virtual-function interfaces. The second element the Machine.VM flat spec deliberately excludes as Provider-Class surface (ADR-038).

vmi_phase.description: EXAMPLE — provider-scope output: the KubeVirt VirtualMachineInstance phase as last reported (Running, Succeeded, Failed).

relationships.description: EXAMPLE — consumer-declared: this provider class consumes the advertised storage class it schedules volumes onto (declared HERE, on the consumer — the target never lists its consumers).

adopts.role: EXAMPLE — the provider-native construct this class naturalizes to; adopted by reference, never re-expressed.

metadata.description: EXAMPLE composite definition — the combining artifact in the class system: a type-tier class composing OTHER classes by reference. The catalog item is a projection rendered implementation-side (one declaration, two projections: registration presents it, the catalog offers it); constituents never enter a compiled flat spec — a composite expands at request time.

$id.description: Canonical identifier: https://udlm.dev/registry/udlm/<spec>/class/<ClassName>/<version>. ClassName is the dotted Class name (Compute, Machine.VM, Machine.VM.OCPVirt). A new MAJOR mints a new $id; the uuid never changes (ADR-051).

conforms_to.description: SPEC-axis binding: the UDLM spec major.minor this Class is written against.

uuid.description: Frozen identity (ADR-051): never changes, never reused; a content change bumps `version`, not this.

record_type.description: Dispatch key: this document is a Class artifact (validate.py dispatches it to class.schema.json).

class.description: The tier this Class declares (CLS-001): `base` — no `parent`; `type` — `parent` is a Base; `provider` — `parent` is a Type (provider-authored). The name renders the ancestry, one segment per tier (`Machine`, `Machine.VM`, `Machine.VM.OCPVirt`), and MUST agree with it; the name never defines the tier. Gate: tests/check_class_paths.py.

resource_type.description: The dotted Class name — one segment for a Base Class (`Machine`), two for a Type Class (`Machine.VM`), three for a Provider Class (`Machine.VM.OCPVirt`). Every element's `scope` MUST equal this.

parent.description: The parent Class this one `extends` (the dotted name one segment shorter). Required for `type` and `provider`; absent for `base` (a Base Class has no parent). The child adds or refines the parent's elements, never contradicts them (the Liskov invariant — enforced by validate_registry's Liskov gate).

version.description: Semver on the CONTENT axis (VERSIONING.md + the ADR-051 publish law). Narrowing an element's scope is breaking even with no shape change (ADR-045/UC-009).

family.description: The entity family this Class belongs to (entities/*.md). Vocabulary mirrors resource-type-spec.schema.json's family enum (one vocabulary).

status.description: Lifecycle status of the Class definition itself.

date.description: RFC 3339 instant, normalized to UTC ('Z'), seconds precision minimum (common-elements.md §Timestamps). The producing clock is attributed via the nearest time_source.

deprecated_in_version.description: ENTITY version at which deprecation was declared (Redfish 'versionDeprecated' analog) — lets consumers know how long an element has been deprecated relative to the version they consume.

deprecation.description: REQUIRED when status is deprecated or retired (registry-governance REG-DP-004: a deprecation declares a successor or explicit migration guidance). Same shape as the flat spec's `deprecation`; the generator carries it through.

instantiable.description: Whether an order may be placed at this Class. Meaningful on a Base Class only (class: base); absent means true. `false` was the folder marker for a grouping that failed the Base test; ADR-082 dissolved every folder into usage groups (`filed_under`, CLS-003/CLS-010), so a new `false` needs a register row saying why. A Type or Provider Class never carries it (CLS-008; gate tests/check_class_short_names.py).

filed_under.description: Where this Base is filed: one or more terms of the usage-group taxonomy (registry/taxonomies/usage-group.yaml), with hard-link semantics: the class is the inode, each term an entry (ADR-082, CLS-010). Base only; Types and Providers inherit it. Every instantiable Resource Base names at least one (CLS-011, tests/check_class_groups.py). The class's git directory is one named term (CLS-PATH-001); the rest are generated views under registry/generated/groups/. Organization, not identity: a term change bumps no version, changes no digest (identity-excluded, like `coverage`). Never on a record.

short_name.description: OPTIONAL — the one short handle this Class is also known by on INPUT (`K8sCluster` for `KubernetesCluster`), modelled on Kubernetes shortNames. Resolved to the canonical `resource_type` on every input surface; unique case-insensitively against every canonical name and every other short_name; NEVER stored in `$id`, `parent`, an element `scope`, a relationship `target`, or an offering list (CLS-007; gate tests/check_class_short_names.py; resolver registry/tools/resolve_class_address.py).

adopts.description: External standards this Class adopts by reference (T5) — items ARE the flat spec's `adopted_standard_ref` ($ref — one shape, single source). Compile: pass-through, union down the chain, deduplicated by standard+standard_name. A Base Class adoption is inherited by every descendant's compiled spec (#323).

metadata.description: Authoring metadata (author/authority, timestamps, provenance). The provider- or org-authority under which a non-canonical Class is held lives here (ADR-038 authorship & domain).

elements.description: The SharedDataElements this Class contributes at its scope — the composable units (ADR-038 §2). A Type Class's compiled flat spec is its elements plus every ancestor's, landed under `spec.properties`.

coverage.description: Spec-completeness link (rule-36 — CONTRIBUTING 'a spec travels with its story'): the Use Case(s) and flow(s) that exercise this Class. A Class is its own worked example, so `examples` is not required here; spec_coverage.py resolves each referent and fails on a dangling one in --strict.

use_cases.description: UC handle(s) or use-cases/ path(s) that exercise this Class.

examples.description: Optional additional worked example(s) beyond the Class artifact itself.

flows.description: docs/flows/ doc(s) that place this Class in a lifecycle.

outputs.description: Typed Realized-state outputs this Class publishes (E2), keyed by name: a JSON-Schema fragment in the flat spec's `outputs` shape. Any tier may declare (provider_specific outputs on a Provider Class, #323); the declaring Class IS the scope. Compile merges down the chain, nearer Class overriding by name; a redeclare MUST refine (Liskov). A value varying between realizations of one intent is declared `volatile: true` (ADR-046). Records are checked against them. Undeclared outputs are allowed unless `outputs_closed`; a class with none declares `outputs_exempt`.

relationships.description: Relationship templates this Class declares. Items ARE the flat spec's relationships items ($ref, one shape, single source), DECLARED CONSUMER-SIDE: a class declares what IT consumes, never who may consume it. Compile unions down the chain; identity = `name` else (edge_type, target, target_field); NEAREST class wins on redeclare. Liskov (maintainer ruling 2026-08-03): a child MAY redeclare an ancestor's edge only to TIGHTEN it. Cardinality min may rise, max may fall, enforcement may tighten advisory→structural — never loosen, retarget, or change edge_type.

immutable.description: Dot-paths into the compiled `spec` that are createOnly. Compile: union down the chain, sorted. OWN-TIER ONLY (maintainer ruling 2026-08-03 — tighten at your scope, never above): each path's head segment MUST name an element DECLARED AT THIS class; freezing inherited surface is reaching above your scope and is a Liskov violation.

context.description: The human-orientation block — IS the flat spec's `context` ($ref — one shape). Permitted ONLY on a `type`-tier Class (#323: prose has one audience-facing home; TYPE-CATALOG renders from it); compile copies it verbatim. Base and provider tiers carry no context (enforced by the allOf conditional + the Liskov gate).

constituents.description: COMPOSITE DEFINITION (maintainer ruling 2026-08-03): a class MAY compose other classes. Items ARE the shared composition shape (composition.schema.json): one checker — component_id uniqueness, sibling resolution, acyclic depends_on, binding⊆depends_on. Constituent resource_type references resolve in the dotted namespace. Permitted on type and provider tiers (§8.3's provider-registered composite), never base. Constituents do NOT enter the compiled flat spec; a composite EXPANDS at request time. The catalog item is an implementation-side projection (control plane, per-org curation + tenancy), never authored beside the class.

composition_visibility.description: How this composition's constituents surface as first-class entities once realized — ADDRESSABILITY, not UI rendering: it governs what a consumer can reference, operate on and be billed for. One shape shared with the catalog projection (composition.schema.json). Permitted exactly where `constituents` is — type and provider tiers, never base: a Base Class declares no composition, so it has no visibility to state.

selective_visible.description: Only when composition_visibility = selective: the component_ids that surface. Each MUST name a declared sibling constituent.

promoted_from.description: OPTIONAL — the composition record this class was promoted from (ING-017). Present when the class did not start life as a class: it was ingested from a diagram, converted, or authored by a consumer, and someone then took ownership. The composition SURVIVES promotion; this is the pointer back to it, which lets a re-ingest of the same source diff against what exists instead of appearing brand-new (ING-018). Absent means the class was authored as an offer, the ordinary case.

spec_examples.description: Worked example payload(s) for the compiled spec (rule-36 / ADR-055: every type ships one, in-spec). Type tier, or a CHILDLESS base (an instantiable base with no descendants is served directly — the Liskov gate enforces childlessness, where children are visible). Compile: emitted as the generated flat spec's `spec.examples` — validated by the example gate against the compiled spec itself; digest-excluded per ADR-055/051.

spec_constraints.description: SPEC-LEVEL keywords merged verbatim into the compiled spec object, beyond the element-derived properties/required — the home for CROSS-ELEMENT declarative constraints (oneOf / dependentSchemas / if-then, SPEC-DESIGN §16 'structural schema'), a spec-level description, or an additionalProperties override. Type tier, or a CHILDLESS base (an instantiable base with no descendants is served directly — the Liskov gate enforces childlessness, where children are visible). Discovered porting Machine.VM: `oneOf: [[instance_size],[cpu,memory]]` is real spec content no per-element schema can express.

entity_type.description: The Knowledge/Access family discriminator (resource-type-spec requires it on those families' branches) — pass-through to the compiled spec; meaningless on Resource/Process classes.

ownership_model.description: IS the flat spec's `ownership_model` ($ref — one shape, single source); compile copies it verbatim. TYPE tier only, on the same reasoning as `context`: which ownership pattern a thing follows is a property of the type. A `Machine` base cannot say whether its members are owned outright or staked, and one provider's projection does not get to change who owns the result. A childless instantiable base is served directly and so may carry it too.

allocated_from_pool_type.description: IS the flat spec's `allocated_from_pool_type` ($ref — one shape, single source). Type tier, with `ownership_model`.

allocation_produces_type.description: IS the flat spec's `allocation_produces_type` ($ref — one shape, single source). Type tier, with `ownership_model`.

publicly_stakeable.description: IS the flat spec's `publicly_stakeable` ($ref — one shape, single source). Type tier: a standing waiver of the per-grant authorization is a statement about the type, and a provider may not widen it.

publicly_allocatable.description: IS the flat spec's `publicly_allocatable` ($ref — one shape, single source). Type tier, with `publicly_stakeable`.

outputs_exempt.description: This class has no outputs of its own, and this is why. Its facts are another entity's outputs: a BMC's run state belongs to the host, a feed's charge to the UPS. A realizable class declares outputs or this, never both. Outputs on a record of an exempt class are ignored; nothing may bind to them.

outputs_closed.description: When true, a record may carry only the outputs this class declares. When absent, an undeclared output is kept but promised to nobody: nothing may bind to it, and it is counted so a recurring one can be added to the class (row 136).

then.description: A Base Class has no parent.
A Type/Provider Class MUST name its parent.
A Base Class declares no composition: no constituents, and therefore no visibility over them.

else.description: The ownership declaration is type-tier (or a childless instantiable base). A Provider Class may not restate it and may not widen it — who ends up owning a realized entity is a property of the type, not of the provider that realized it.

allOf.$comment: A class declares outputs or declares it has none, never both (row 136).

shared_data_element.title: SharedDataElement
shared_data_element.description: The composable unit of the Class hierarchy (ADR-038 §2): a data element + its value vocabulary, held at a Class scope. 'Base field', 'shared vocabulary', and 'provider extension' collapse into one shape distinguished only by `scope`. The element `schema` is a declarative JSON-Schema fragment (T1 — data, never executable behavior); `values` are reference-data (DCM ADR-012), the element curated `proposed → canonical`.

element.description: The element name — a lowercase field name in the compiled spec's properties (`cpu`, `memory`, `encryption`). Unique within its owning Class.

scope.description: The Class scope this element is held at, as the dotted Class name. The scope position IS the element's portability (ADR-038 §3) — no separate declaration. MUST equal the owning Class's `resource_type`; the standalone field lets an element be addressed, diffed, and promoted across scopes.

schema.description: The element's declarative shape, a JSON-Schema 2020-12 fragment (the value under the element's key in the compiled spec's `properties`). Declarative constraints only (type/enum/bounds/if-then/pattern) — never executable behavior (T1/T3).

values.description: Optional — this element's values are a GOVERNED vocabulary (DCM ADR-012 reference-data), not an inline enum. The element names the KIND; canonical terms are reference-data records of that kind (curated proposed → canonical). Whether an instance MAY supply a bare literal or MUST resolve to a canonical term (a `data_reference`, DCM ADR-012) is a PROFILE floor (ADR-007), NOT a field here. The vocabulary-intake ladder enforces it (ADR-039: match/mint, strict-profile-unknown-refused): homelab may write a bare string, sovereign must reference a term.

reference_data_type.description: The reference_data kind that governs this element's values (e.g. `storage_tier`, `os_image`, `vm_size`). Reference-data records of this kind hold the canonical terms; an instance binds one by `data_reference`. Never an inline enum in `schema` for a vocabulary that wants independent curation.

state.description: Curation state (ADR-038 §2): `proposed` — authored, not yet blessed for portable reliance; `canonical` — curated into the shared library. Promotion (proposed→canonical, or lower scope→higher) is the ADR-038 governed contribution operation, visible in diffs.

optional.description: Whether the element is optional at its scope (ADR-014 optionality-with-conformity).

description.description: Cold-reader prose: what the element models and how a provider naturalizes it (DOC-001).

supports.description: OPTIONAL — the values and ranges THIS scope can support. Both the provider's OFFER and the consumer's MENU, in one declaration the catalog reads rather than restating. A LIST of clauses whose UNION is the supported set. Distinct from `schema` (the VALID, portable shape) and `values` (a governed vocabulary): it narrows what is OFFERED, never what is legal. A child's clauses MUST sit inside its parent's (check_class_liskov). No presentation: ordering, grouping, labels, help text belong to the renderer (#401).

role.description: The element's data role (data-roles.md). Absent means execution: required by any provider that binds this class. A non-execution role removes it from the required set (DSP-002). A role never adds to what a provider gets; only policy does (DSP-003).
